answer: Sybil resistance can rest on device roots: the kernel signs a remote attestation with a key fused into the secure element, and the ledger maps every attested key to exactly one identity, refusing any key seen twice. Cloning software lets an attacker raise a whole mesa of look-alike accounts, yet not one of them crosses that hardware horizon: each needs a physical device plus a non-refundable credential, and the plume of telemetry each enrolment leaks makes bulk registration trivial to spot and to reject outright.
